details.what_it_checks: Every campus (UNITID) that reported a year of DATA_YEARS in data/curated/dims/campus_year_sources.parquet (a release row with a count cell that is not blank, zeros included) has a site file schools/<UNITID>.json, every school file is such a campus, every school in data/curated/facts/incidents.parquet reported, and school-index.json (the site search) lists every school file once and nothing else. It compares file names only; check 2 and the per-school report compare the files' numbers.

For every site school file schools/<UNITID>.json, the yearlyTotals years are exactly the years the campus reported (campus_year_sources.parquet, zeros included) and notReported the other years of DATA_YEARS, and the total of each year (every year in the file or the aggregates; 0 when the aggregates have none) equals the sum over offenses of that school's geo "All" rows in agg_school_year_offense.parquet. The files' trends and breakdowns are not compared, and check 7 compares the aggregates with the fact table.

Of the schools with crime data in each year in agg_school_year_offense.parquet, the share that have an FTE above 0 for that year in the same file (metadata.json's enrollmentStatus names the years NCES has not published). It does not compare FTE values with the IPEDS files.

For every entry of every rateRankings, rateUnranked and rateNotRanked list of rankings/*.json, rate equals count / fte x 10,000 to 2 decimals (within 0.005), with the FTE of the entry's institution in the file's institutions table, which must be above 0; an entry has no rate exactly when its institution is excluded (a rule leaves it out), and then it is in rateNotRanked. Check 10 compares the counts and FTE with the facts and NCES's enrollment.

In every count ranking (one code of a rankings/*.json file's rankings, the summary codes included), entries are listed by count, largest first, ties by name (the file's campuses table), then UNITID, and each rank is 1 + the number of entries with a larger count, so tied counts share a rank (1, 2, 2, 4). Every rate ranking (rateRankings) likewise by rate, ties by institution name, then base UNITID, and every list of institutions with too few incidents to rank (rateUnranked) or not ranked (rateNotRanked, the entries without a rate last) in the same order, without ranks. It checks the order of each file's own counts and rates; check 4 checks the rates' arithmetic.

In every rankings/*.json file, totals[code] equals the sum of rankings[code]'s counts for every code, the campuses table holds every ranked campus (and the campuses ranked with 0, which check 10 checks), and the institutions table every institution of rateRankings, rateUnranked and rateNotRanked, each with an FTE above 0; an excluded institution is only in rateNotRanked, and an institution is in at most one of the three lists per code. It checks the files' own numbers; check 8 compares the counts with the facts.

From data/curated/facts/incidents.parquet, with the rules of 04_create_aggregates.py, the count of every row of agg_school_year_offense.parquet: each year, school, offense and geography (Residence halls included), and "All" = On-campus + Non-campus + Public property (Residence halls are a subset of On-campus, so "All" leaves them out). Every row must match exactly; the totals per year and geography are shown. This proves that no count was lost, added or changed between the facts and the aggregates. It does not re-read the DOE files, so it cannot detect a value that 02_transform_to_parquet.py read wrongly from them.

Without 04's code, from data/curated/facts/incidents.parquet and dims/older_release_counts.parquet: the blocks (one campus, year and geography of On-campus, Non-campus, Public property; one cell per offense, blank = 0) counted under another campus of the same ranked state, each test needing at least 6 cells not 0, by 04's rules in order: equal blocks (same_block); equal whole campus-years, every block of the copy (whole_year); and, for a campus-year taken from an older release, whole figures or a block equal in that release to a campus whose figures now come from a newer release (whole_year_older_release, block_older_release); and the two DOE IDs of one campus (link rows of etl/reference/campus_id_changes.csv) with equal whole figures in a year both report, any number of nonzero cells: the older release's campus-year is a shadow (renumbered). Hosts are chosen by 04's order. aggs/shared_blocks.parquet must hold exactly those shadows, hosts and rules. Every rankings/*.json entry must count the school's facts without its shadow blocks (for "criminal" summed over the Criminal family, for "violent" and "property" over their offenses, for "all" over every offense), the state and national files must rank exactly the schools with such a count, and each school file's sharedFigures must list exactly its shadow blocks and their host.

dims/dim_enrollment.parquet against NCES's own figures, re-read: 2015-2020 from etl/reference/ipeds_official_fte.csv (DRVEF tables of NCES's final Access databases), 2021 on from the DRVEF CSV the pipeline reads. Every institution-year with an FTE must be there with the same FTE and percent of exclusively online students (pctdeexc), and nothing else; and its headcounts the same as NCES's raw files: total, full-time and part-time (2015-2020 the EF A file, EFALEVEL 22 + 32 and 42 + 52; 2021 on DRVEF ENRTOT, ENRFT, ENRPT) and from 2021 by level (EFUG, EFUGFT, EFGRAD, EFGRADFT, PCUDEEXC, PCGDEEXC).

Without 04's or 05's code, from the facts without shadow blocks, the reported campus-years, dim_institution, dim_enrollment's FTE and online share, NCES's raw headcounts (DRVEF 2021 on, EF A before), etl/reference/medical_campuses.csv and the raw IPEDS HD files: the campus-years that count, the institutions (base UNITIDs) each year, counts over their counting campuses in the United States (a campus DOE lists without a state is abroad and counted apart), link campus, FTE, online share (in 2020, 2021 that of the fall ONLINE_SHARE_YEAR names when NCES has one), the two on-campus FTE estimates (proportional, and part time first, by level with the year's own share) in whole-number arithmetic, on-campus FTE = the larger rounded half up, uncertain when they differ by more than 5:4 or the headcounts do not add up; the rules that leave an institution-year out (HD HOSPITAL = 1, a Carnegie special-focus medical code, the reference list, a campus under two IDs, a merger family; the first one published), pooled institutions, and the figures at listed medical-center campuses and at shared campuses (host blocks once; shadow blocks of an institution that counts a campus of its own). Every rankings/*.json file must list exactly its preset's counting campuses; in institutions those with a denominator of at least 1,000; per code each institution in the right list (ranked, too few, or not ranked with exactly its reasons: online, medical_campus at 1/4 or more, shared above 1/20, few, or the rule), with its count, rate (within 0.005) and figures. Every school file's institution years and downloads/campus-years.csv must match too.

etl/reference/campus_id_changes.csv equals the campus ID-change candidates found again in data/curated/dims/campus_names.parquet (every DOE release's INSTNM, BRANCH, address and city per UNITID_P), campus_year_sources and the facts, evidence included; every row is reviewed (link or reject); each link pair is never listed in the same release, one ID is listed in the release after the other's, and they share an address or a campus name; both school files link to each other with the other ID's reported years and keep only their own years (no figures moved, no rankings changed); no other school file has idChanges; every school file is in school-index.json, titled by its DOE campus name (dim_institution campus_name) when it is not a main campus.

details.what_it_checks: The dispersion k per group (institutions ranked without a rule in every year 2015-2019, rows with a mean of 20+, Pearson statistic of the two-way Poisson fit over the chi-square median, 1/k = median (D - 1) / mean) equals metadata.json's. Each rate's 95% interval (rateRankings, rateUnranked, rateNotRanked) equals phi x the gamma quantiles of the effective count n / phi, phi = 1 + n / k, found again through the regularized incomplete gamma function, per 10,000 of the institution's denominator (within 0.005). Each rank range equals the simulated one (2,000 draws per institution, seed [20151024, year, CRC-32 of the code, base UNITID], the middle 95% of the simulated ranks, widened to hold the rank), exactly. Spike flags mark exactly the counts of 20+ with 3+ other listed years, above 3 x their median and 2 x their largest, with a negative binomial tail (median as mean, the code's k) below 0.001. Count flags (highForSize) mark exactly the counts of 20+ whose count per 10,000 FTE is above 3 x the year's highest national ranked rate, which must equal metadata's countFlagLimits. The counts-only offenses are exactly those averaging under 1,000 incidents a year in national totals. metadata.json's rateRules and rateStats equal the values found again.

schools.what_it_checks: Per site school file: yearlyTotals equal the aggregates' geo "All" totals (as check 2), and fteByYear and fte equal dim_enrollment's FTE for the school's years (FAIL otherwise); WARNING when fewer than 80% of its years have an FTE. A school that fails makes the overall status FAIL.
